facts.value: Cognitive psychology involves the study of mental processes, including perception, attention, language comprehension and production, memory, and problem solving.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Researchers in the field of cognitive psychology are sometimes called cognitivists.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Cognitivists rely on an information processing model of mental functioning.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Cognitivist research is informed by functionalism and experimental psychology.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Starting in the 1950s, the experimental techniques developed by Wundt, James, Ebbinghaus, and others re-emerged as experimental psychology became increasingly cognitivist and became part of the wider, interdisciplinary field of cognitive science.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Some called this development the cognitive revolution because it rejected the anti-mentalist dogma of behaviorism as well as the strictures of psychoanalysis.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Albert Bandura helped along the transition in psychology from behaviorism to cognitive psychology.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Bandura and other social learning theorists advanced the idea of vicarious learning.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Technological advances renewed interest in mental states and mental representations.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Charles Sherrington and Donald O. Hebb used experimental methods to link psychological phenomena to the brain's structure and function.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: The rise of computer science, cybernetics, and artificial intelligence underlined the value of comparing information processing in humans and machines.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: A popular and representative topic in this area is cognitive bias, or irrational thought.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Psychologists and economists have classified and described a sizeable catalog of biases which recur frequently in human thought.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: The availability heuristic is the tendency to overestimate the importance of something that happens to come readily to mind.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Elements of behaviorism and cognitive psychology were synthesized to form cognitive behavioral therapy.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Cognitive science is an interdisciplinary enterprise involving cognitive psychologists, cognitive neuroscientists, linguists, and researchers in artificial intelligence, human–computer interaction, and computational neuroscience.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: The discipline of cognitive science covers cognitive psychology as well as philosophy of mind, computer science, and neuroscience.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Computer simulations are sometimes used to model phenomena of interest.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
